newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares weighed down by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares weighed down by Wall Street.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower, weighed down by U.S. market losses, but local dealers said that sentiment at home was good and the market was ripe for a rebound.
"Even though the market is positive it was not enough to outweigh external influence, but the Danish market didn't fall as much as the major European markets," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index fell 0.47 point to 131.15 in slack overall bourse turnover of 444 million crowns. The KFX December future fell 1.35 point to 130.70 with 149 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Most activity was outside the top 20, where football club Brondby's share rose over 50 percent to close at 250 crowns in turnover of 33,000 shares traded.

The share's popularity followed the team's sensational 5-0 away win over Germany's Karlsruhe on Tuesday, putting the team in the quarter final of the UEFA cup and promising bigger gate receipts at home.

Carlsberg fell eight crowns, to 377, on what dealers said were rumours on the Stockholm bourse that its Royal Copenhagen unit planned to sell some of its packaging business to Sweden's PLM.--Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969653
